key_insight: Optimized flux pulses enable 12-ns transmon CZ gates with intrinsic errors near 2×10⁻⁵, while identifying operating regimes resilient to dephasing.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps balance gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness, potentially reducing characterization and recalibration overhead in scalable superconducting processors.
method: Optimize smooth, single-shot flux pulses for directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons.
Model intrinsic Hamiltonian errors, energy relaxation, and fast and slow dephasing.
Identify dephasing sweet spots and exploit transmon asymmetry for noise resilience.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 12-ns gates near an 11.6-ns theoretical speed limit and intrinsic errors around 2×10⁻⁵, using dephasing models calibrated against published experimental measurements.
watch_item: The reported intrinsic error excludes decoherence contributions, and the abstract does not report experimental validation of the optimized gates.
paper_title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
